## Natural history notes

A semi-aquatic mammal characterized by its long streamlined body, dense brown fur, webbed feet, and thick tapering tail. In Florida, it is found in rivers, streams, lakes, ponds, marshes, swamps, and coastal wetlands with access to water and nearby cover. It is an active swimmer and predator that feeds mainly on fish, crayfish, frogs, and other aquatic animals, often using dens along banks, roots, or shoreline vegetation.
